artists.biography: Stevland Hardaway Morris, known professionally as Stevie Wonder, is an American singer-songwriter, musician, and record producer. He is widely regarded as one of the most influential musicians of the 20th century, and is credited as a pioneer and influence by musicians across a range of genres that include R&B, pop, soul, gospel, funk, and jazz. Wonder's use of synthesizers and other electronic musical instruments in the 1970s reshaped the conventions of contemporary R&B. He also helped drive such genres into the album era, crafting his LPs as cohesive and consistent, in addition to socially conscious statements with complex compositions.

perplexity.description:
Stevie Wonder’s The Definitive Collection, released in 2002 by Motown and UMe, is a career-spanning compilation that showcases the breadth of his musical genius across four decades. The album features 21 tracks, highlighting Wonder’s mastery of Funk, Soul, and R&B, with occasional forays into reggae-inflected grooves such as “Master Blaster (Jammin’)”. The collection traces his evolution from early Motown hits like “Fingertips (Part 2)” and “Uptight (Everything’s Alright)” to his groundbreaking 1970s classics including “Superstition”, “Living For The City”, and “Sir Duke”, as well as later hits such as “Part-Time Lover”. Wonder’s signature blend of melodic sophistication, lyrical depth, and innovative use of synthesizers and rhythm is on full display throughout.

As the first single-disc anthology to comprehensively cover Wonder’s career up to that point, The Definitive Collection holds a significant place in his discography, serving as both an introduction for new listeners and a concise retrospective for longtime fans. The album received strong commercial success, reflecting Wonder’s enduring popularity, and was praised for its thoughtful track selection and sound quality. While not a new studio release, it was widely regarded as an essential summary of one of popular music’s most influential careers, capturing the essence of his impact on Funk, Soul, and beyond.
